title: What Even Is Trading?
hook: Trading isn't predicting the future. You're participating in price movement.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should understand what a trade actually is — before strategies, charts, or indicators enter the conversation.

beats.heading: Buy, sell, or short
beats.body: Trading is participating in a financial market by taking a position based on the expectation that price will move. Buy and price rises, or sell/short and price falls — either way there's potential profit. But if price moves against the position, there can be a loss.

beats.heading: Long vs. short
beats.body: Going long means you're positioned to benefit if price rises. Going short means you're positioned to benefit if price falls. Futures let you do either from the start — you don't have to "buy first" like traditional investing.

beats.heading: Trading vs. investing
beats.body: Investing generally focuses on owning an asset and participating in its longer-term growth. Trading generally focuses on profiting from price movement over a defined period. Neither is inherently better — they're different activities.

beats.heading: Trading isn't prediction
beats.body: Our job isn't to know exactly what the market will do next. Our job is to interpret the information price gives us and make rule-based decisions.

blocks.heading: The four pieces of every trade
blocks.prompt: Tap the four pieces in order.

items.label: Direction
items.desc: Do you expect price to rise or fall?

items.label: Risk
items.desc: Where are you wrong, and how much are you willing to lose?

items.label: Outcome
items.desc: Price moves. Your position gains or loses value.

blocks.successFeedback: That's the full shape of a trade — market, direction, risk, outcome.
blocks.failFeedback: Close — think about what you'd decide first: what you're trading, then which way, then your risk, then the outcome plays out.

blocks.quote: You don't need to know what happens next with certainty to trade. Later, you'll learn to build a thesis, wait for confirmation, and define exactly what would make that thesis invalid.

questions.question: A trader believes MNQ is likely to decline and takes a position designed to profit from falling prices. What kind of position did she take?
questions.why: A position designed to profit from falling prices is a short — you're positioned to benefit when price falls.

questions.question: A trader's analysis supports higher prices, but price moves against the position. Which statement best represents the AGHF mindset?
options: A thesis can be reasonable and still be wrong; risk defines what happens next
The analysis must eventually become correct
Add another position to improve the entry
Wait until price returns to entry
questions.why: Being reasonable and being right aren't the same thing — that's exactly why risk is defined before the trade, not decided emotionally after.

blocks.prompt: Think about it: Why is "I think price is going up" not a complete trading plan? What's missing from that statement?

takeaways: Trading is participating in price movement, not predicting the future.
Going long profits from price rising; going short profits from price falling.
Every trade has four pieces: market, direction, risk, and outcome.
remember: Trading isn't about being certain. It's about making structured decisions under uncertainty.
